seo_title: Cibolo Christmas Events for Kids 2026: 2 Events, 1 Free
seo_desc: 2 Christmas events for kids in Cibolo, TX for 2026, 1 free: Holidays on Main: Holiday Parade and Tree Lighting and Christmas in Bethlehem Living Village.
lede: Cibolo puts its Christmas on Main Street: the city rolls its holiday parade, vendor market and tree lighting with Santa into one day called Holidays on Main, and a local church builds a free walk-through Bethlehem village each December.
celebrates: The City of Cibolo combined its two favorite holiday traditions into one celebration called Holidays on Main. The day opens with the annual Holiday Parade, with floats from elected officials, community partners and local organizations rolling down Main Street to City Hall. After the parade, families head to the plaza at Pfeil Road and Main Street for a holiday vendor market with local artisans, food trucks, live entertainment and family activities. The evening ends with the official tree lighting and Santa Claus. Each December, Everyday Christian Fellowship also opens Christmas in Bethlehem, a free living village with more than twenty stops, animals and cocoa.
lastyear: In 2025, Holidays on Main fell on Saturday, December 6. The parade stepped off at 11 am with a Cowboy Christmas theme, starting at Borgfeld Road and Cibolo Valley Drive, heading down Main Street and ending at City Hall. The vendor market ran from 3 to 7:30 pm at Main Street and Pfeil Road. DJ BSquared hosted performances by Mary Lou's Dance School, the LoneStar Dance Crew and the Steele High School Chorus, then a 6 pm countdown to the tree lighting and pictures with Santa at 6:15 pm.
facts: Cibolo is named after Cibolo Creek, and the city says cibolo is an Indian word meaning buffalo. According to the city's history, the railroad asked a local businessman, Mr. Schlather, to name the town, and he chose Cibolo. Residents voted to become an independent town on October 9, 1965. The U.S. Census counted 440 people in 1970, and by 2023 the city estimated 37,061. The Holiday Parade is now past its twelfth year.
trains: Cibolo's history is usually counted from 1876, the year the Southern Pacific Railroad cut through town and linked it to Houston and San Antonio. That line was built as the Galveston, Harrisburg and San Antonio Railway, which reached nearby Marion in the spring of 1876. Today the nearest Amtrak stop is the San Antonio station on Hoefgen Street, next to the former Southern Pacific Sunset Station, served by the Sunset Limited and the Texas Eagle. Train fans can also visit the San Antonio Railroad Heritage Museum in Elmendorf or ride the Hill Country Flyer from Cedar Park.

faq: What is Holidays on Main in Cibolo?

Holidays on Main is the City of Cibolo's one-day holiday celebration. It joins the annual Holiday Parade, a Holiday Vendor Market at the plaza at Pfeil Road and Main Street, and the official tree lighting into a single day. Families can watch the parade, shop local artisans and food trucks, enjoy live entertainment and see Santa after the tree is lit.
Where does the Cibolo holiday parade go?

In 2025 the parade started at Borgfeld Road and Cibolo Valley Drive, continued down Main Street and ended at Cibolo City Hall at 200 South Main Street. The city shares the parade map, parking areas and road closures closer to each year's event, so check the Holidays on Main page before you go.
Where can kids see Santa in Cibolo?

Santa Claus joins the City of Cibolo's tree lighting at the plaza at Main Street and Pfeil Road during Holidays on Main. In 2025 pictures with Santa started right after the 6 pm tree lighting countdown. Families can also meet St. Nicholas at a booth in Christmas in Bethlehem at Everyday Christian Fellowship.
Is there a live Nativity in Cibolo?

Yes. Everyday Christian Fellowship at 950 Everyday Way hosts Christmas in Bethlehem, a free walk-through re-creation of Bethlehem from the city gate to the manger. It has more than twenty stops, including the Nativity, an animal pen, candle making and a children's area, plus free cookies, cocoa and s'mores.
How did Cibolo get its name?

The city says Cibolo was named after Cibolo Creek, which flows through the area, and that cibolo is an Indian word meaning buffalo. The story goes that the railroad asked local businessman Mr. Schlather to name the town in 1876, when the Southern Pacific Railroad came through, and he chose Cibolo.
Where is the nearest Amtrak station to Cibolo?

The nearest Amtrak station is in San Antonio at 350 Hoefgen Street, next to the former Southern Pacific Sunset Station. Amtrak's Sunset Limited and Texas Eagle stop there. Cibolo is about 13 miles east of the San Antonio metro area, according to the city.
